value.body: Helps a factory, plant or project site follow environment, health and safety (EHS) rules. Manufacturing, chemical, pharma, construction and infrastructure companies hire EHS staff. A day can include site inspections, checking effluent and waste records, preparing compliance reports and supporting audits or safety training.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc Environmental Science or Chemistry, or a B.Tech
items.note: A diploma in industrial safety is often asked for in safety-focused roles

items.label: Rules you work with
items.value: Pollution control consents, hazardous-waste rules, factory safety rules

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join as EHS trainees or executives in plants and project sites, often via campus or job portals. Knowledge of pollution control consents, waste rules and ISO 14001 basics helps; a recognised industrial-safety diploma is required for many statutory safety-officer posts.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Working with plant teams and auditors

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is at the plant or site, sometimes in shifts.
Growth path: executive → EHS officer → EHS manager for a site or region.
Roles differ: some lean to environment compliance, others to safety.
